chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade eating the flesh of the stallion at the time of its heat.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating stallion meat during its heat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes a specific prohibition (nahy) on consuming the meat of a stallion during its rutting season (aghtilamuhu), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the purity and quality of food sources. The ruling is attributed directly to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and transmitted through a reliable chain including al-Sakuni, highlighting the practical application of dietary laws in early Islamic jurisprudence. This prohibition underscores the concept of 'khabith' (impure or undesirable) in food, linking physical state to spiritual and legal permissibility.
